## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Fix the containment check in `preview` before merge: it compares paths only as text, so a relative argument such as `../secret.txt` passes the check and the function reads a file outside the home directory. This review read the full diff, `app/paths.py`, and `tests/test_paths.py`; it did not run the tests. The change to `settings_file` and its test are correct as written.

## Changes
The pull request adds `preview(home, relative)`, which returns the first 200 characters of a file under the home directory and raises `ValueError` for paths outside it. It also adds `settings_file(home)`, tests for both functions, and a one-line text file, `tests/review-note.txt`.

## Critical
- app/paths.py:12 — correctness — Resolve paths before the home containment check — Calling `preview(home, "../secret.txt")` passes the check and reads `<home>/../secret.txt`, which is outside home. `Path.is_relative_to` compares path components as text and does not collapse `..`, so `Path(home) / "../secret.txt"` still starts with `home`'s components. A symlink inside home that points elsewhere also passes. The only negative test (`tests/test_paths.py:20`) uses an absolute path outside home, which fails the check for a different reason, so the traversal case is never tested. — Any caller that passes a user-supplied relative path can read any file the process can access, up to 200 characters per call; this is the exact case the `"outside home"` guard exists to block. — Fix: Compare resolved paths: `base = Path(home).resolve(); candidate = (base / relative).resolve(); if not candidate.is_relative_to(base): raise ValueError(...)`. Add tests for `"../outside.txt"` and for a symlink inside home that points outside it.
